newsitem.title: UK: European PC sales growth slows in first quarter.
newsitem.headline: European PC sales growth slows in first quarter.

text.p: By Neil Winton, Science and Technology Correspondent

Sales growth of personal computers in Europe lost momentum in the first quarter, held back by stagnant conditions in France and a lacklustre reception for the latest Intel Pentium MMX technology, a survey published Friday said.

The outlook for the whole of 1997 looks uncertain, according to market researcher CONTEXT, with consumers worried about their prospects. Sales should probably turn out to show about the same growth as last year.
COMPAQ Computer Corp of the U.S. retained its market leadership at 14.7 percent in the first quarter, up from 12.3 percent in the same period last year.
Direct seller Dell Computer Corp with 5.7 percent, jumped three places to fourth. Siemens Nixdorf's 5.8 percent saw it jump two places to third.
CONTEXT said that western European PC sales grew a modest 9.9 percent in the first quarter to 4.34 million, down from a 13.6 percent increase in the same period last year.
For all of 1996, sales growth slowed to 11.5 percent, compared with a 25 percent increase in 1995.
"We are saying that growth for 1997 will be between 10 and 12 percent. But if anything that is a bit optimistic," said Emmanuel Lalloz, senior PC research analyst at CONTEXT.
"Consumer markets are slowing down because of the economic recession, and purchasing power is being squeezed by increasing taxes to help governments meet the Maastricht (single currency) criteria."
"France looks particularly worrying with the corporate market closing down and consumer markets drying up," Lalloz said.
Sales in France grew only 0.7 percent in the quarter to 865,000.
Of the other major markets, Britain grew 12.2 percent to 960,000. but this was slower than expected. In Germany, sales rose 8.8 percent to just over one million.

Scandinavian markets were strong, with Sweden up 17.3 percent, Norway up 25.5 percent, and Denmark 13.0 percent higher. Benelux sales also impressed with the Netherlands up 17.0 percent and Belgium 25.2 percent to the good.
"COMPAQ is doing well with its portable products after launching the Armada last year," said Lalloz, "while Dell's reliance on governments and business helped it."
"Companies like (direct mailer) Gateway 2000 and Packard Bell which rely on consumer markets were finding conditions tougher," Lalloz said.

Lalloz said that sales of Pentium MMX processor-equipped PCs had been disappointing, while some customers were holding back purchase decisions awaiting Intel's new Pentium 2, to be launched next week.
